subdimensions.name: Suffering Detection

evidence.quote: Thailand is damaging its reputation by complying with Chinese government requests to unlawfully deport Chinese dissidents.

subdimensions.note: Thailand runs a Universal Coverage Scheme reaching near-universal population health detection, and immigration authorities keep records on detainees; but the four UNHCR-recognised refugees at Suan Phlu Immigration Detention Center were identified by HRW, not by a Thai protection pathway.

subdimensions.name: Contextual Sensitivity

evidence.quote: Thailand is damaging its reputation by complying with Chinese government requests to unlawfully deport Chinese dissidents.

subdimensions.note: Thailand differentiates services for migrant workers, hill-tribe populations and the elderly, but applies a uniform detention regime to recognised refugees regardless of protection status.

subdimensions.name: Blind Spot Mitigation

evidence.quote: Successive Thai governments have found it easy to cast aside Thailand's international obligations to please Beijing.

subdimensions.note: No structured process for identifying protection gaps; HRW notes the pattern is repeated across successive governments rather than corrected.

subdimensions.name: Signal Amplification

evidence.quote: Thailand should demonstrate that it has earned its membership on the UN Human Rights Council.

subdimensions.note: UNHCR and HRW amplify detainee concerns externally; there is no domestic structural role with authority to escalate them.

evidence.quote: Fighting in July 2025 killed and injured civilians, including children, displaced around 300,000 people, and damaged religious and cultural sites.

subdimensions.note: No published pre-decision harm assessment before deportation or before the border escalations of 2025.
